item: A long gate hold in the storage-events journal carries what its holder thread was doing in the kernel (ws, gap), counted once a second from /proc, paid for by writing frames at their measured width
refs: coordinator 17 Oct; OSM gate census REPORT section 2
summary: The 16 Oct holds of 30 to 182 s could not be told apart as slow work or a stalled thread. holder_state looks at the holder once a second while a hold is past 30 s and already journaled (3 small /proc reads, 29 microseconds, on the watchdog thread) and counts six classes: running, runnable, futex, nap (SQLite's busy handler), disk, other; gap is the longest time between two looks. The first look counts nothing (it is the baseline); the thread's name and the kernel symbol are never kept; off Linux the hold says ws null with ws_why unsupported-os; counts reach the journal at the 15 s tick and at the release, not once a second. futex is a floor for GIL waits (a look hands the GIL to its only waiter). Bytes: 57 per hold at the widest (+14 for the ws_why null a cleared reason leaves), and 827 in the method, paid by writer.FRAME_CHARS = 79, the measured maximum of module:function:line under src/, pinned both ways against every function by an AST walk (it was 90 in the first cut, 11 characters nothing had measured), which frees 4,740 bytes the model counted for frames no real event has; the widest journal is 123,749 bytes with all 20 splits (1,251 free; ordinary names 83,779), the fixed part 5,176 to 6,003. Also fixes a flake: the phase tests counted samples of the module's gate while the process's own watchdog thread could tick in the same hold (about 8 per cent of runs).
